To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) for the exceptional Laguerre polynomials, the zeros are real, distinct, and interlaced with the zeros of the classical Laguerre polynomails, and (ii) for the exceptional Jacobi polynomials, the behavior of the zeros is more complicated.

the zeros of the exceptional 𝑌l Jacobi polynomials are all real for all 𝑙, and the zeros of the 𝑌1 and 𝑌2 Jacobi polynomials have a very special structure: they are symmetric with respect to the origin and the real axis, and their absolute values increase monotonically from the origin.

(i) the zeros of the 𝑋l Jacobi polynomials are all real and distinct, (ii) the zeros of 𝑋l+1 are interlaced with those of 𝑋1,2,…𝑋l and 𝑋l is the only exceptional Jacobi polynomial that has a zero of multiplicity 2, and (iii) the zeros of all 𝑋l (l=1,2,…) are interlaced.

the zeros of the exceptional 𝑛l Jacobi polynomials and the zeros of the 𝑛l Laguerre polynomials with 𝑛=1,2,3,… and l=1, 2, ….

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
these exceptional polynomials are not exceptional in any way.
these exceptional Laguerre and/or Jacobi polynomials are very similar to the classical Laguerre and the Hermite polynomials, respectively.
the zeros of the exceptional 𝑙th Laguerre and 𝑙th Jacobi polynomials, for l=1,3,5,…, behave in the same way as the zeros of the classical 𝑙th orthogonal polynomials.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the zeros are not sensitive to the changes in the parameter of the Hamiltonian.
the zeros are distributed in a way which resembles the zeros of the classical Laguerre and Gegenbauer polynomials.
the zeros of exceptional Laguerre and/or Jacobi polynomials tend to cluster around some points, which depend on the parameters of the Hamiltonian, as the number of zeros increases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the exceptional Laguerre and exceptional Jacobi polynomials are very special in their own right and deserve more attention.
, in contrast to the classical orthogonal polynomials, the zeros of the exceptional polynomials are not confined to a single interval.
the zeros of these new polynomails are very different from those of the classical orthogonal polynomials.
